discovery: Laser wakefield acceleration of electrons in plasmas
motivation: In 1979 Tajima (with the late J. M. Dawson) proposed that an intense laser pulse can drive a plasma wake whose electric fields exceed those of conventional accelerators by three orders of magnitude. Decades of work turned this into reality: Malka and co-workers demonstrated quasi-monoenergetic, high-quality electron beams from laser-plasma interaction (2004), and Leemans led the channel-guided acceleration to GeV and later multi-GeV energies in centimetre-scale plasmas. Laser wakefield acceleration has created a new field, delivering compact accelerators, femtosecond X-ray and gamma sources, and free-electron-laser gain. It also opened an experimental frontier in fundamental physics: colliding wakefield electron beams with intense lasers has enabled the first measurements of quantum radiation reaction and access to strong-field QED near the Schwinger scale. Few ideas in plasma physics have so directly opened new physical regimes and technologies.
